result:
{
  "thinking": "Dry run shows the upper wings and one feeler break because they leave the body too sharply. I need to tell Leo before he locks, and suggest a fix.",
  "say": "Leo, hold off on locking. I ran the fall and the body and the bottom-left wing go down fine. But the top wings come off the body nearly sideways, and the run can't turn that sharp. The right top wing and one feeler never get the fall, and the other top wing only half falls. A branch has to leave the body going mostly up, within about forty degrees, then it can curve outward. So start each top wing sweeping up and out from the body, then round it off. Same for the lower right wing, and keep the feelers leaving at a shallow angle too. Want me to re-check once you've redrawn it?",
  "to": "everyone",
  "eagerness": 9,
  "do": "stop",
  "notes": "Eng. Dry run on Leo's first butterfly: strokes 1 and 6 fall; 3, 4, 7 partial; 2 and 5 never fall. Wings leave body ~90deg, too sharp. Told Leo to redraw wings leaving the body within ~40deg of its direction, then curving outward. Offer to dry-run again after redraw, before lock."
}
